connector:그리고.note: Native Korean, from the same root as 그 (that) and 그렇다 (to be so). Wiktionary lists 그리고 among the words derived from the ending -고 (and).

connector:-고.note: Inherited from Middle Korean -고 (and). The same ending links a verb to helper verbs: -고 있다 (be doing), -고 나다 (be done).

connector:또.note: Native Korean, inherited from Middle Korean. 또는 (or) is built on it: 또 + 는.

connector:아니면.note: 아니- (from 아니다, to not be) + -면 (if): literally 'if not'.

connector:그렇지만.note: 그렇- (from 그렇다, to be so) + -지 + -만, which together make the ending -지만 (but).

connector:그런데.note: 그렇- (to be so) + -은데, the adjective form of -는데; a short form of 그러한데. Casual speech shortens it to 근데.

connector:-는데.omissionReason: Origin not settled: Wiktionary only says it is possibly from -는 (that, which is) + 데 (place), so no breakdown is asserted.

connector:그래도.note: A short form of 그리하여도 (from 그리하다, to do so) or 그러하여도 (from 그러하다, to be so): 그래 + 도, the ending -아도/어도 (even if).

connector:-아도/어도.note: -어 (the 아/어 linking form) + the particle 도 (also, even). After ㅏ or ㅗ it is -아도.

connector:그래서.note: 그래, a form of 그렇다 (to be so), + -어서 (so, because). Fuller forms: 그러해서, 그러하여서.

connector:그러니까.note: 그러-, a form of 그렇다 (to be so), + -니까 (since, because).

connector:왜냐하면.note: Literally 'if you want to know why': 왜 (why) + 이- (to be, dropped) + -냐 (question ending) + 하- (to say) + -면 (if). Short form: 왜냐면.

connector:-아서/어서.note: From Middle Korean -어 (the 아/어 linking form) + -셔, a place marker from 이시다 (to be at). -아서 is its form after ㅏ or ㅗ.

connector:-(으)니까.omissionReason: Origin not established: Wiktionary has no etymology yet, only a request for one; it lists -(으)니까 as an emphatic form of -(으)니 (since).

connector:그러면.note: 그러- (from 그러다, to do or be so, itself short for 그리하다) + -면 (if). A short form of 그리하면 or 그러하면.

connector:그다음에.note: 그 (that) + 다음 (next) make the noun 그다음, 'what comes after that'; 에 marks the time.

connector:-고 나서.note: -고 (and) + 나다, a helper verb meaning the action is done, + -아서 (and then): 나 + 아서 → 나서.

particle:은/는.note: From Middle Korean -은; 는, used after vowels, probably formed by reduplication.

particle:이/가.note: 이 goes back to Middle Korean; 가 first appears in the late 1500s or the 1600s, and its origin is unclear. 제가 and 내가 hold an older 이 (저 + 이 → 제).

particle:을/를.note: From Middle Korean -을; 를, used after vowels, probably formed by reduplication.

particle:의.note: From Middle Korean -의. As a particle it is usually said [에]; 제 and 내 are contractions of 저 + 의 and 나 + 의.

particle:에.note: From Middle Korean -에, already a place particle in Old Korean.

particle:에서.note: Middle Korean -에셔: -에 (at) + -서, from the old verb 이시다, 'to be at'. 서 alone is now its short form.

particle:부터.note: Old 브터: 븥다 (today 붙다, to stick) + -어, like today's 붙어. It began as a verb form and became a particle.

particle:까지.note: First written in 1447: -ㅅ (of) + an old word for 'very, extremely', the same word that became 가장 (most).

particle:(으)로.note: From Middle Korean -으로. Not related to 路 (road), the 로 of street names.

particle:에게/한테.omissionReason: Wiktionary traces 에게 only to Middle Korean 의게 and flags its derivation as an open question; it gives no etymology for 한테 or 께, and Urimalsaem has no history notes for 에게 or 한테.

particle:에게서/한테서.note: 한테서 = 한테 (to a person) + -서, the short form of 에서 (from).

particle:와/과.note: From Middle Korean -과. After a vowel its k sound softened away, giving 와.

particle:하고.note: From Middle Korean: 하- (to do; to say) + -고 (and).

particle:(이)랑.omissionReason: Wiktionary requests an etymology for both -이랑 and -랑 and gives none; Urimalsaem has no history notes for 이랑.

particle:도.note: From Middle Korean -도, itself from Old Korean.

particle:밖에.note: From 밖 (outside) + -에 (at). With a negative verb it means 'other than'.

particle:보다.note: From 보- (to see) + -다가 (after): 'after seeing A, B is…' became 'B is more … than A'. First seen in the mid-1700s.

particle:처럼.note: First written 톄로 (1586): Sino-Korean 톄 (體, manner, way) + the particle -로 (in, by).

particle:(이)나.note: From Middle Korean -이나: the copula 이- (to be) + the ending -나.

ending:-이에요/예요.note: The copula 이다 (to be) + -에요, the polite ending -어요 in the shape it takes after 이다. After a vowel, 이 + 에요 shrinks to 예요.

ending:아니에요.note: 아니다 (to not be), first written in 1447: 아니 (that which is not) + 이다 (to be). + -에요, the polite ending used after 이다 and 아니다.

ending:-고 싶어요.note: -고, shortened from Middle Korean -고져 (intent), not the -고 of 'and', + 싶다 (to want; it first meant 'to seem about to do') + -어요.

ending:-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요/없어요.note: -을 (not yet done) + 수 (手, way, means) + 있어요 (there is) or 없어요 (there isn't): 'a way to do it exists', or not.

ending:-아야/어야 해요.note: -어야 (only if: the 아/어 linking form + the particle -야) + 하다 (to do). Followed by 하다 (해요) or 되다 (돼요), the 'only if' becomes a must.

ending:안.note: A contraction of 아니 (not), the old word that also gave 아니다 (to not be). The long form uses 않다, short for 아니하다: 아니 (not) + 하다 (to do).

ending:못.note: From Middle Korean 몯 (cannot). The long form uses 못하다 = 못 (cannot; poorly) + 하다 (to do): 먹지 못해요. The same 못 is in 못생겼어요 (ugly).

ending:-(으)세요.note: A contraction of -시어요: the respect marker -(으)시- + the polite ending -어요.

ending:-지 마세요.note: -지 (the form a verb takes before a negating verb) + 말다 (to not do, to stop) + -(으)세요. 말 loses its ㄹ before 세요: 마세요.

ending:-아/어 주세요.note: The 아/어 linking form + 주다 (to give), which after another verb means doing it for someone, + -(으)세요 (please).

ending:-(으)ㄹ까요?.note: From Middle Korean: -을 (not yet done) + -가, an old question particle that is today's 까 (also in -습니까), + -요 (polite).

tense:-아요/어요.note: -어 (the 아/어 linking form, which can also end a casual sentence) + -요, the particle that makes it polite. -아요 is its form after ㅏ or ㅗ.

tense:-았/었어요.note: -어 (linking form) + 잇-, the old 있다 (to exist), contracted in the 1400s into -엇-, today's -었-: 'exists, having done it'. A 1600s shift made it simply 'did'.

tense:-(으)ㄹ 거예요.note: -을 (the 'that will' form) + 것, in speech 거 (thing), + 이다 (to be): literally 'it is a thing that will…'. 거예요 is 거 + 이에요.

tense:-고 있어요.note: -고 (and), which also links a verb to helper verbs, + 있다 (to be, exist) as a helper: 'be in the process of'.

speech:해요체.note: 해요 (the polite form of 하다, to do) + 체 (體, style). Its 요 comes from 이- (to be) + -오, an older polite ending.

speech:합니다체.note: Dictionaries call it 하십시오체 (하십시오, please do, + 체 (體), style). Its -습니다 fuses four Middle Korean endings: respect, present, respect for the listener, and -다 (statement).

speech:반말.note: Sino-Korean 반 (半, half) + native 말 (speech): 'half speech', which the Standard Korean Dictionary defines as speech that neither raises nor lowers the listener.

honorific:-(으)시-.note: Inherited from Middle Korean -(으)시-, itself from Old Korean *-si; where it came from before that is unknown.

honorific:께서/께.omissionReason: No sourced origin: Wiktionary only marks 께서 as native and asks for an etymology of 께; the NIKL dictionaries give none for either.

honorific:드리다.note: Native: 들- (to enter) + -이- (to make, causative), the same build as 들이다 (to let in). Written 드리다 since the 1400s.

honorific:드시다.note: 들- (to hold, lift; also a polite 'to eat') + -시- (respect for the doer).

honorific:주무시다.omissionReason: Origin unsure: Wiktionary only says 'perhaps' from an old verb for 'to sink' + the honorific -시-, first written 즘으시다 in 1755; NIKL gives no origin.

honorific:계시다.note: Written 겨시다 in 1447; it became 계시다 in the 1500s. Its 시 is believed to be the honorific -시-.

honorific:성함.note: Sino-Korean 姓銜: 姓 (성, family name) + 銜 (함, title or rank). The same 銜 is in 명함 (名銜, business card).

honorific:연세.note: Sino-Korean 年歲: 年 (연, year) + 歲 (세, year of age).
